data.name: Crazy Otto
data.detailed_description:
In 2016's CRAZY OTTO you and up to seven of your friends have a job to do. Run the maze, eat the dots, grab the cake, dodge the dinosaurs.

Unless you are the dinosaurs, in which case you'd better eat CRAZY OTTO and his friends!

At long last, this very special home edition of the greatest arcade machine never made is coming to a video games system near you! What makes it so special? Not only are we bringing you all the thrills of the arcade original, but we've bulked it up to TWENTY-FIVE LEVELS, making CRAZY OTTO the biggest game of all time!

And that’s not all! We’ve added the ability for up to EIGHT SIMULTANEOUS PLAYERS to take control of not just Otto and his friends, but of the baddies that are trying to stop them from eating everything in the maze!

CRAZY OTTO is a real treat for the whole family!

  • Classic dot-eating, maze-navigating action!
  • Play as the goodies or the baddies!
  • Twenty-five levels - more levels than in any other game ever!
  • Up to eight simultaneous players!
  • Full support for vertical monitors, for that real arcade feel!
  • Localised for Spain, Germany, Russia and China!

reviews.review:
Crazy Otto is a charming tribute to classic arcade gaming, combining familiar maze-based challenges with an entertaining multiplayer concept. Developed and published by Extend Mode, the game embraces the simplicity of traditional dot-collecting adventures while adding competitive elements that make it particularly enjoyable with friends. Rather than introducing complicated systems or elaborate storytelling, it concentrates on quick reactions, strategic movement, and accessible entertainment. Its nostalgic presentation and playful personality make it appealing to enthusiasts of old-school arcade experiences, although its relatively limited gameplay variety prevents it from achieving the depth of more ambitious modern releases.

The central gameplay involves guiding Otto and his companions through enclosed mazes while collecting dots and cakes scattered throughout each stage. Dangerous dinosaurs patrol the environments, creating obstacles that players must avoid while completing their objectives. Although the controls and mechanics are straightforward, navigating efficiently requires careful timing, anticipation, and awareness of enemy positions. Players must decide whether to pursue nearby collectibles or retreat when approaching enemies threaten to trap them. This balance between risk and reward creates enjoyable moments of tension, particularly when escaping dangerous situations with little room to maneuver.

The game's most distinctive feature is its support for up to eight simultaneous players, allowing participants to control either the protagonists or the dinosaurs pursuing them. This unusual arrangement transforms a traditional arcade formula into a competitive multiplayer experience where human opponents introduce unpredictable behavior. Players controlling the dinosaurs can coordinate their movements to intercept opponents, while those controlling Otto and his allies must develop strategies to avoid capture. The resulting interactions can be entertaining, especially when several friends participate. Local multiplayer and Steam Remote Play Together further enhance its accessibility as a casual party game.

Crazy Otto includes twenty-five levels, providing a collection of mazes that encourage players to improve their navigation skills and experiment with different approaches. The straightforward objectives make the experience easy to understand, while the presence of pursuing enemies maintains a reasonable level of challenge. However, the gameplay does not evolve dramatically as players progress. The limited mechanical variety and repetitive objectives can reduce long-term engagement, particularly for those who prefer substantial progression systems, unlockable abilities, or more elaborate challenges. Its structure is better suited to shorter gaming sessions than extended solo play.

Visually, the game adopts a minimalist retro aesthetic inspired by early arcade machines. Its colorful characters, simple maze layouts, and uncomplicated presentation prioritize clarity over graphical sophistication. This artistic direction complements the gameplay by keeping collectibles, pathways, and enemies recognizable. Support for vertical monitor orientation is a particularly appealing feature for enthusiasts interested in recreating the appearance of traditional arcade cabinets. Although the graphics may seem outdated to players accustomed to modern visual effects, their simplicity contributes to the game's nostalgic atmosphere.

The overall presentation also benefits from a playful sense of humor. Its exaggerated promotional descriptions enthusiastically celebrate familiar arcade features, giving the game a self-aware personality. The unusual combination of dinosaurs, collectible cakes, and maze-chasing competition reinforces its lighthearted identity. There is little emphasis on narrative development or character backgrounds, but the absence of storytelling does not significantly undermine an experience built around immediate arcade action. Instead, its entertainment comes from mastering movement, completing objectives, and competing against friends.

Crazy Otto is officially rated Playable on Steam Deck, not Unknown or Unverified. Its default controller configuration supports the game's functionality, and performance is considered satisfactory. However, some controller icons may not match Steam Deck buttons, and external controllers may require manual selection through the Quick Access Menu.

Despite its enjoyable multiplayer possibilities, Crazy Otto has noticeable limitations. Its reliance on established arcade mechanics means that much of the experience feels familiar, while the relatively small selection of gameplay variations limits its lasting appeal. Solo players may find the repetition particularly noticeable without the unpredictability introduced by human opponents. Nevertheless, its approachable design, nostalgic presentation, and competitive structure provide enough entertainment for players seeking an uncomplicated arcade diversion.

Overall, Crazy Otto delivers a pleasant combination of retro charm, accessible gameplay, and entertaining multiplayer competition. Its greatest achievement is allowing players to experience both sides of the traditional maze-chasing formula, creating opportunities for amusing confrontations and friendly rivalries. Although its limited depth and repetitive structure prevent it from becoming an essential arcade title, it remains a worthwhile option for enthusiasts of classic gaming and casual multiplayer entertainment. 

Rating: 6/10
